title: check: same signature re-verified by ssh-keygen many times
description:
_verifies (git-vouch:914) runs one ssh-keygen -Y verify per call and makes a TemporaryDirectory with two files each time, with no memo. One run measured about 9 ms. The same (data, sig, namespace, key) is verified again and again:
(a) verify_person runs on each person file's origin version at git-vouch:1450, then again on every version, origin included, in the warning loop at 1711-1716.
(b) judge() is memoized per (handle, position) at 1771-1779, not per record content. tier_at(approver, a) for every grant (1849), standing(handle, p) at each parent of each adding commit (1897-1902, 1916-1917) and held_at all reach judge_tier at fresh positions where the tier bytes are unchanged, and each one reaches check_signer -> verify_approval -> ssh-keygen.
(c) _signer (937) tries candidate keys one ssh-keygen run at a time, so verify_person with previous+own keys costs up to k runs per block.

Estimated (not measured) at kernel scale: about 6,000 ssh-keygen runs per check, about 55 s. The distinct signatures are about 606 person + 606 tier + 1,800 endorsement, about 3,000 runs or 27 s, which is the floor without a persistent cache.

What goes wrong if it stays: about half of check's ssh-keygen time is spent re-proving facts already proven in the same run.

Fix: a module-level dict in _verifies keyed by (data, sig, namespace, key.ssh) covers (a) and (b) in about 4 lines and keeps ssh-keygen as the only verifier. For (c), read the signer's public key from the SSHSIG blob (its second wire string, parsed by the existing _ssh_strings) and verify against that one candidate only. That is parsing, not cryptography, so the 'no cryptography in this file' rule holds. The ponytail at 937 should then go.
